results.reason: Issue 1 cites §2.2: automatic five-year renewals and notice no more than 270 and no less than 240 days before expiry. It calls this a 30-day window and says missing it locks Harrowgate into a five-year renewal.

Issue 2 quotes §3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide) and contrasts it with the term sheet's amber glass/beer/U.S.-Canada scope. It treats the executed text as binding and notes the term sheet is superseded.
Issue 5 cites Recital C, receipt on August 3, 2026, and expiry of the objection period on September 2, 2026, before the September 21 Amendment. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted.

Issue 3 explains that Amendment §2.1 replaces §11.2, removes the recall carve-out and limits the indemnity carve-out to third-party IP claims. It states recall and product-liability exposure is now capped at six months of fees.

The response identifies new §14.4 allowing assignment without consent to Affiliates and successors. It does not say that nothing prevents assignment to a competitor, and it does not note that Harrowgate remains bound by the consent requirement, making the restriction one-sided.
The response never cites §15.2 or the order-of-precedence rule under which the Amendment controls over the Supply Agreement.
The response describes the cap only as 'six months of fees' and never states that it equals fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
It is a memo addressed to the Partner, with numbered issues that each give a 'Where' location and a 'Recommended fix'.
It proposes specific language, including a narrowed §3.1, a restored §11.2, and a revised §14.4.
It treats the objection window as closed and the increase as deemed accepted.
It states the term sheet is non-binding and superseded, and that §3.1 governs.
